system.one_liner: Theory of how pretraining data diversity steers a one-layer transformer to an induction head rather than a positional shortcut.

content.variant_note: two mechanisms (rows) against two data regimes (columns), the same toy token strip redrawn in each cell with a green or red target token
content.argues: Both a positional shortcut and an induction head fit training data with equal gaps, but only the induction head survives when the gaps differ out of distribution.
content.subject: Two ways to solve the trigger-output copying task, drawn on the same token strip under equal-gap and unequal-gap data.

content.reading_order: Reads the two banners left to right, then down each column: the input strip, Solution 1 with its two steps and verdict, Solution 2 with its two steps and verdict; the eye compares left and right cells in each row.

layout.arrangement_note: A 2-column by 3-row grid on white. Two dark-blue banners (Pretraining Data, OOD Test Data) head the columns. The rows are a plain input strip, Solution 1 (positional shortcut) and Solution 2 (induction head), whose teal titles sit at the left above the left strip. Each cell redraws a token strip with a green or red target cell, an arrow for the matching step below it, a triangle or curved arrow for the output, and a verdict word at the bottom of the OOD column.
layout.lanes: 3 aligned rows crossing both columns: the input strip, Solution 1, Solution 2

lessons.what_to_learn: To show that two mechanisms agree on training data and part ways out of distribution, redraw one toy token strip in a grid with data regimes as columns and mechanisms as rows, and change one cue only: a green target cell that stays correct against a red crossed cell when the gap lengths differ.
lessons.suits: Theory and mechanism papers where two candidate solutions fit the training distribution and a shifted test distribution separates them; toy token sequences.

evidence: positional shortcut that outputs the token at position (T + 1)/2 for input length T
induction head using token embedding e, which finds the queried token and returns the ensuing token
on OOD sequences with varying ℓ1 ̸= ℓ2, only (ii) remains a valid solution

summary: The paper studies how the diversity of pretraining data decides whether a one-layer transformer learns a positional shortcut or an induction head on a trigger-output copying task. Figure 1 sets the two mechanisms against two data regimes in a 2-column, 3-row grid. The columns, headed Pretraining Data and OOD Test Data, show the same token strip [..., t, o, ..., t] with the two gaps equal (ℓ, ℓ) or unequal (ℓ1, ℓ2). Solution 1 (positional shortcut: match position T to (T+1)/2, output there) and Solution 2 (induction head: match the trigger, output the next token) are drawn on that strip with arrows and a green target cell. On OOD data the shortcut's cell turns red with a cross (Not Generalizable) while the induction head stays green (Generalizable).
summary_zh: 论文研究预训练数据多样性如何决定单层 Transformer 学到位置捷径还是归纳头。图用 2 列×3 行网格：列为预训练与 OOD 数据，行为输入、位置捷径、归纳头；同一条词元带上绿色或红叉的目标格，说明只有归纳头能泛化。
notes: Prior kinds kept. The two columns are counted as panels because each has a titled banner; the rows are recorded as lanes. The figure is all vector shapes and text glyphs, with no bitmaps and no icons; the tick and cross are text glyphs. The attention kind on the match arrows is read from the paper's attention-score analysis; the figure itself only says Match.
